dependencies.note: At Ethereum block 26239007, 90.44% of fxUSD supply sat in the f(x) Stability Pool. fxSAVE redemption can release that locked supply into circulation and pays a smaller USDC leg directly. DexTracker's October 20 fxUSD-to-USDC quote observed USDC proceeds peaking near $4.27M; this is a dated limit on the fxUSD route, not a ceiling on the entire fxSAVE redemption basket. Consumer registration should be checked before assuming this overlay renders.
dependencies.upstream_resolution_rule: ⚠️ EVERY upstream entry MUST carry exactly one resolution: `slug` (one asset we score), `slugs` (a set entry naming several), `terminal: true` + `kind` (never scoreable — oracle, venue, contract, authority, incentive, real-world), or `unresolved` (scoreable, no report yet = COVERAGE GAP). ⚠️ TERMINAL AND UNRESOLVED ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS and must never be merged: terminal means nothing is missing, unresolved means a report is owed. `address` is REQUIRED wherever the ticker collides in this corpus (DUSD x4, msUSD x3, reUSD x2, USD3 x2, BOLD x2) — a ticker-keyed graph would merge Resupply's reUSD (3.5) with Re Protocol's (5.0).

downstream_basis.asserted_only_note: None — every asserted edge is reproducible from an upstream array.
downstream_basis.do_not_hand_edit: ⚠️ downstream_tracked is GENERATED. Hand-maintaining both directions is how fxsave came to list fxUSD as BOTH its upstream and its downstream — one edge recorded twice, in opposite directions. Add the edge to the UPSTREAM array of the dependent asset and re-run build.
